solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stormy southern trip curtailed in Norwegian waters

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters that follow are churned into a new order
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter of trip goes

parts.note: the word as printed, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A rough voyage south is cut short somewhere off the coast of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts trip to TRI; with SOUTHERN that gives eleven letters for 'Stormy' to rearrange. North Utsire is one of the sea areas named in the BBC Shipping Forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: This shipping-forecast sea area lies off the south-west coast of Norway, so it names Norwegian waters.

clue.text: Religious woman holding a church degree with distinction

indicators.note: holding means the religious woman surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a nun is a woman in a religious order
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun with a church qualification graduates with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with distinction' suggests an honours degree but means fine shades of difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuanced view draws subtle differences, so it is marked by fine distinction.

clue.text: Say one unionist is taken in by eminent scientists under royal patronage?

indicators.note: taken in by means the following pieces sit inside the scientists' letters

parts.note: RS is the Royal Society, Britain's academy of leading scientists
EG, for example, means say
I is the Roman numeral for one
U is a short form of Unionist in British politics

explanation.surface: A unionist is welcomed among distinguished scientists who enjoy the Crown's support.
explanation.walkthrough: Regius professorships at old British universities are chairs founded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regius is Latin for royal, applied to professorships established by royal endowment.

clue.text: United in no more than wordless singing without a sense of fun

parts.note: to hum is to sing without words

indicators.note: in means the united letter goes inside the phrase meaning no more than

parts.note: or less, as in ten or less, means no more than
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A team joins in a quiet hum, sung without much enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humourless lacks the ability to laugh, having no sense of fun.

clue.text: (Description of unfinished) business?

definitions.meaning: jobs still pending are said to be on a list of things yet to tackle
a fuss or commotion, as in what a business

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket marks the first reading: work left to be done. Read whole, 'business' is the other: a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss, and tasks yet to complete are on a to-do list.

clue.text: Not quite the done thing, if daring in execution

indicators.note: in execution means as the letters are carried out or performed, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something is slightly improper if it is boldly carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' hints at a hanging but means the act of performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means beneath one's dignity, unbecoming.

clue.text: Runs into bar for a bit

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pub for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract from a text or film, a small bit of it.

clue.text: Magazine priest rejected showing a mixture of things

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the magazine-plus-priest string is read backwards

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A periodical turned down by a clergyman is a hotchpotch of articles.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination of different elements, a mixture of things.

clue.text: Take heart, after he's ditched non-representational style

parts.note: to abstract is to take away or remove

indicators.note: ditched means thrown out, so those letters leave the word heart

parts.note: the pronoun as printed, with 's meaning has

explanation.surface: An encouragement to cheer up after a man has been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's ditched' removes HE from heart, leaving ART.
explanation.definitionFit: This art form does not depict real objects, so it is non-figurative in style.

clue.text: Bound to include third of receipts if reversing shortfall

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole assembled string is then read backwards
to include means the bound word takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: bound as in tied up

indicators.note: third of picks out the third letter of the word receipts

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to count receipts if a cash shortage is to be turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts CIF inside TIED to give TICIFED, and 'reversing' then turns all of it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is the amount by which something falls short, a synonym of shortfall.

clue.text: Rebuilding won't work, interrupting unsettled sleep for urban dwellers

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting the letters together again in a new arrangement

parts.note: the contraction's letters, with the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: interrupting means the work piece breaks into the shuffled sleep letters
unsettled means the letters are disturbed into a fresh order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Building works that refuse to finish keep disturbing a restless night's sleep for city folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' makes SPELE of sleep; 'work' is OP from the Latin opus, the usual label on a composer's numbered works.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of a town are its residents, those living in an urban area.

clue.text: Evil spirit to act like vampire, mostly with youngsters around university

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a vampire sucks blood

indicators.note: around means the young animals' word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: cubs are young animals, or young Scouts

explanation.surface: A demon that drinks blood like a vampire, accompanied by a pack of young students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SUCK to SUC.
explanation.definitionFit: A succubus is a female demon of folklore, a classic evil spirit.

clue.text: Mate's to spoil water trip

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
a row is an outing in a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A friend is set to ruin a boating excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Mate's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a marrow is a companion or workmate, a pal.

clue.text: Encountered actor excited about King and I — one appreciates ability

indicators.note: about means the word for encountered goes round the following letters

parts.note: met means encountered
R is for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: excited means the letters of actor are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone met a thrilled performer from The King and I, a fan who values talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is a musical, but here King is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in meritocracy wants advancement based on talent, so values ability.

clue.text: No lover of ribaldry — lacks playfulness, initially abusive

indicators.note: lacks means goes without, so a letter is removed from the prim person

parts.note: a prude disapproves of bawdy humour

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letter of the word playfulness

explanation.surface: A prim person without any sense of fun is, at first, offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes the P (the first letter of playfulness, picked by 'initially') from PRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and abusive are synonyms for insulting, offensive language or behaviour.

clue.text: Soothes everyone: takes new course, ousting leader

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter is thrown out

parts.note: to deviate is to take a different course

explanation.surface: Something calms everybody as it changes direction and drops its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting leader' trims DEVIATES to EVIATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or distress is to ease or relieve it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Think about mother's source of fragrance

indicators.note: about means the thinking word wraps round the mother

parts.note: to ponder is to think
ma is mother, the 's being possessive

explanation.surface: Consider what perfume your mum wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball of scented spices or an orange stuck with cloves, giving off a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Banner promotes this development of process in incorporating hospital

indicators.note: incorporating means the rearranged letters take in another inside them
development of means the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone who bans things favours a procedure that takes place within a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banner' is read as one who bans, not a flag. 'development of' rearranges PROCESSIN and 'incorporating' puts H among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bans books or films champions suppression of material, the very practice of censoring.

clue.text: Unseemly row during endless recess in city

indicators.note: during means the rearranged row sits within the trimmed recess
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a niche is a recess in a wall

indicators.note: unseemly means improper or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An improper argument breaks out during an interminable break in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NICHE to NICH, and 'Unseemly' makes ORW from row. Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is the county town of Norfolk and a cathedral city in England.

clue.text: Soldier's end in battle providing shock

parts.note: man is a common crossword word for a soldier, as in officers and men

indicators.note: end in picks the final letter of the word battle

explanation.surface: A soldier dies in combat, which comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like distress at death but means a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick bushy mass, as is a mane, a crossword-friendly synonym.

clue.text: Metal figure, notice, encapsulating sculpture of Rodin?

indicators.note: encapsulating means the notice word encloses the next letters

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: a sculpture is a shaping, so Rodin is moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A bronze statue with a plaque around a Rodin sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was a French sculptor, apt for metal figures; 'sculpture of' turns his name into NDROI.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look like a person, a metal humanoid figure.

clue.text: Marine creature's hum pervading ocean? Not quite

indicators.note: pervading means the smell spreads within the trimmed ocean word
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sea as a synonym of ocean
hum and pong are both British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A sea creature's smell fills the ocean, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' looks like a sound but is slang for a stink. 'Not quite' cuts SEA to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is a simple aquatic animal living on the sea floor.

clue.text: A fenland lake overseas

parts.note: the Broads are shallow lakes in the flat fen country of Norfolk and Suffolk

explanation.surface: A lake in East Anglian fen country is described as being abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of lakes and rivers in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to a foreign country, the same as overseas.

clue.text: Given extra power, very much increased power after due changes

indicators.note: after places the power letter behind the rearranged letters

parts.note: so as in so tired, very much
up means increased, as prices are up

indicators.note: changes means the letters of due are rearranged

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Something given a boost has greatly increased power once dues have altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges DUE as EDU.
explanation.definitionFit: A souped-up car has been modified to give more engine performance, extra power.

clue.text: This is some house, mister!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An estate agent boasts to a client: what a house this is, sir!
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the answer itself, which the rest of the clue describes as a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour, as the clue's house is.

clue.text: Drivel bringing one in for a trivial manoeuvre

indicators.note: one in for a means the numeral letter takes the place of the letter A

parts.note: twaddle is nonsense, drivel
the letter A as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nonsense is introduced to justify a petty little move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing one in for a' swaps the A of TWADDLE for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A twiddle is a small twist or turn, an idle little movement of the fingers.

clue.text: Children's author exercised a little

parts.note: ran, as in went for a run to exercise
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A writer for children took a little exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome is best known for his sailing adventure books written for young readers.

clue.text: Material in a red shirt, we fancy

indicators.note: fancy, as an adjective meaning elaborate or decorated, signals reworking the letters

explanation.surface: Someone admires fabric in a scarlet shirt they rather like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb meaning like, but it signals the rearrangement. Harris Tweed is a handwoven woollen cloth from the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This tweed is a famous woollen cloth, so it is an example of material.
